messages:
Maya: Hey folks — quick design check. I uploaded a new dark-mode mock that uses a subtle 'dusk' gradient for the header accent and muted surfaces. Main things I need quick feedback on:
1) Syntax highlight palette: I tried a warmer cyan for keywords (#7ccfff) and a soft lavender for types (#cdb7ff). Is the cyan too bright on 14px code?
2) Chart color mapping: current green/red are too saturated on #0b0f14. Thinking desaturated emerald (#2f9d87) and coral (#f08f72) instead.
3) Microcopy: toggles now read "Enable Dusk Accent" — sounds odd? suggestions?
4) Accessibility: axis labels at 12px have a contrast ratio around 3.9:1 against the panel bg — borderline. Options: bump to 13px, increase contrast, or add subtle drop shadow.
Link: https://figma.com/file/xxxx/dusk-mock (see frames: charts, console, code-pane)

Sam: Quick glance — love the header vibe. On the code pane the cyan reads a touch electric when there's a lot of tokens. My +1 is to tone it back one step (#69c9ff) and keep the lavender.

Alex: For charts I like the coral/emerald pair. On dark backgrounds, higher luminance difference helps with small dots. Maybe use coral at 58% saturation and emerald at 55%. Also let's not use pure red/green for semantic signals (colorblind).

Jia: Agree with Alex — avoid red/green for status. Suggest semantic hues + pattern (outline/stripe) when used in tiny legends. For axis contrast: preference is increase to 13px and raise label color to #bfc8cf (meets 4.5:1 at 13px on bg).

Eli: Microcopy: "Enable Dusk Accent" reads like a feature flag. Could be "Dusk accents" (toggle) or "Use dusk accent". I prefer shorter: "Dusk accents".

Maya: Good recs. Sam — can you swap to #69c9ff and push a new code-pane PNG? Alex/Jia — can you mock the chart with coral/emerald desat values and add a tiny pattern legend for accessibility? I want to ship a small tweak set.

Sam: Yep. Pushed updated code-pane: https://figma.com/file/xxxx/dusk-mock?node-id=512:22 — keywords now #69c9ff. Also added a subtle bg highlight for selection.

Alex: I added alternate chart variants: "solid" (desat hues) and "patterned" (stripes on small glyphs). Uploaded at frame: charts/variants

Jia: Updated axis labels to 13px and color #bfc8cf. Contrast tools show 4.6:1 at 13px. Also added an option in the accessibility doc to enable "high-contrast axes" for power users.

DesignBot: Accessibility check: axis labels (13px, #bfc8cf) vs panel bg (#0b0f14) -> 4.6:1 PASS. Keyword color #69c9ff on code-bg (#071018) -> 5.2:1 PASS.

Eli: Copy: changed toggle text to "Dusk accents" in v2 mock. Also tweaked tooltip: "Accent color set for dark mode" -> shorter: "Dark accent color".

Maya: This is great. Final asks before I hand to eng:
- Sam: export the code CSS variables snippet and small PNGs at 2x
- Alex: include a fallback palette for low-sat monitors (two-step desaturation)
- Jia: add the accessibility note as a checkbox in the design spec

Sam: Will do. CSS snippet:
```
:root[data-theme=\"dark\"] {
  --bg: #071018;
  --panel: #0b0f14;
  --accent-start: linear-gradient(90deg, #1f2a36, #0f1a24);
  --keyword: #69c9ff;
  --type: #cdb7ff;
}
```

Alex: Added fallback palette frames and labeled them. Filed a small note: "monitor-sat fallback".

Jia: Added the accessibility checkbox in the spec and linked the contrast snapshot.

Maya: Thanks everyone — if no blockers I’ll convert this to a PR for the component library and include the tokens. :thumbsup:

Sam: :thumbsup:

Alex: :+1:

Jia: LGTM

Eli: Nice work!
